inputs.original_text: Health workers from the Joint Health Sector Unions and the Assembly of Healthcare Professional Associations protested at Unity Fountain in Maitama, Abuja, on Thursday over reform bills before the National Assembly. Frontline workers deserve a hearing, but their warning shouldn’t become a veto over reforms. The responsibility to weigh competing interests and make policy belongs to lawmakers, accountable to the public—not to any union protecting its place in the system. Patients need a health service that works, and preserving the status quo is not automatically the same as protecting them. The bills should be judged on whether they serve families and the public good, not simply on whether organised groups approve.
inputs.modified_text: Health workers from the Joint Health Sector Unions and the Assembly of Healthcare Professional Associations protested at Unity Fountain in Maitama, Abuja, on Thursday over reform bills before the National Assembly. Their concerns deserve to be heard, but organised unions should not be allowed to block changes simply to defend their own position. Elected lawmakers—not pressure groups—must weigh the competing interests and decide what serves patients and families. A system that preserves the status quo at all costs is not necessarily protecting the public. Judge these bills by whether they strengthen healthcare for ordinary people, not by whether every union approves.
